articles.title: Manchester City found guilty of breaking Premier League’s financial fair play rules
articles.summary: City face sanctions after more than 100 rule breaches. Club insists it is innocent and is expected to appeal. Manchester City face substantial sanctions from the Premier League after an independent panel found they had acted in bad faith and broken numerous rules over financial fair play.
body: The Premier League did not issue a statement but sources confirmed to the Guardian that City had been found guilty on almost all of more than 100 charges. City are surprised at the timing of the news because they say the process is ongoing. It is understood the club intend to appeal against a guilty verdict, confident of winning.

A verdict has been reached more than three and a half years after 134 charges, which cover the seasons 2009-10 to 2022-23, were brought by the Premier League and more than two years since arbitration hearings began. From season 2009-10 to 2022-23 inclusive City won seven Premier League titles, a Champions League, three FA Cups and six League Cups.
Premier League clubs were told of the outcome at Thursday’s shareholders’ meeting and made to sign non-disclosure agreements.

A City spokesperson said: “The Premier League process remains ongoing, with significant elements to be completed, and subject to strict confidentiality. As such Manchester City FC’s position remains consistent with the club’s statement of February 2023.
points: City face sanctions after more than 100 rule breaches.
Club insists it is innocent and is expected to appeal.

articles.title: Mauricio Pochettino regrets not being ‘more involved’ with Balogun decision
articles.summary: US striker had red card ban suspended for Belgium game. Trump said he called Infantino asking for review. Coach says ‘energy of everything’ changed in moment. US men’s national team head coach Mauricio Pochettino has said he regrets not being “more involved” in the situation surrounding US forward…
body: Balogun was given a red card after a challenge against Bosnia and Herzegovina defender Tarik Muharemovic, which by rule is accompanied with a one-game suspension. Balogun’s ban for the next game against Belgium was suspended after the US Soccer Federation and Donald Trump lobbied Fifa, with Trump saying that he personally placed a call to Fifa president Gianni Infantino to ask the ruling be reviewed. Infantino maintains that the decision to reinstate Balogun was made independently by Fifa’s disciplinary committee.

The entire affair cast a pall over what had been an otherwise positive tournament for the US to that point. Belgium’s players and coaches said in the wake of the decision that it provided extra motivation ahead of the match. Balogun himself later spoke of having felt uncomfortable with the attention the situation placed upon him.
Speaking with broadcaster Andrés Cantor on Thursday, Pochettino said he was not involved in the decision – though in retrospect, he may have preferred to be.

articles.title: Palmer misses too many opportunities to play for England
articles.summary: Thomas Tuchel has said that Cole Palmer "misses too many opportunities" to play for England after the Chelsea forward pulled out of the latest squad.
body: The withdrawal of Palmer came as a surprise as he has started all five of Chelsea's matches in the Premier League so far this season, though Tuchel says he had been playing with "discomfort and pain".
The 24-year-old was left out of the World Cup squad by Tuchel and has featured just three times since the German took charge of the Three Lions in January 2025.

"My understanding is that he is playing with discomfort and pain, and he cannot compete at the highest level with discomfort and pain. So he withdrew and informed us, and Chelsea informed us." Tuchel said.
"For sure. It is a missed opportunity. He misses too many opportunities. I don't blame him for it. It is just a fact.

articles.title: How Will Brewers Rotation Line Up For NLDS Amid Questions About No. 3, No. 4 Starter?
articles.summary: The Milwaukee Brewers have secured the No. 1 seed in the National League, and their focus is now on preparing for the National League Division Series. The Brewers will play the winner of the Wild Card Series between the National League's No. 4 and No. 5 seeds.
body: In all likelihood, the Brewers will start Jacob Misiorowski in Game 1, Logan Henderson in Game 2, Robert Gasser in Game 3 and go with a bullpen game in Game 4, if needed, leaning on Dustin May, Sane Drohan or Chad Patrick as bulk options. The Brewers would have Misiorowski on five days of rest for Game 5 if it gets there.

Gasser has been one of the Brewers' best starters in September, but May has the postseason experience. The Brewers may roll with May on a short leash in Game 3, but one of them will need to step up and answer the call. Regardless, similar to last season, Pat Murphy could lean on his bullpen heavily in a game where he does not feel comfortable with his starter. Last season, the Brewers really only had Peralta, but this year they have Misiorowski and Henderson.

articles.title: 'They changed the plan' - Hamilton left frustrated by Ferrari tactics
articles.summary: Lewis Hamilton expressed frustration with Ferrari's approach to Q3 after qualifying sixth for the Azerbaijan Grand Prix, saying "they changed the plan".
body: Hamilton questioned why the team completed only one run of multiple laps at the end of the final knockout stage rather than go out earlier for initial laps, as Mercedes, McLaren and Red Bull with Max Verstappen had done.

The seven-time world champion said his final laps were compromised by having no 'tow' from a car in front to aid straight-line speed down Baku's long main straight. Team-mate Charles Leclerc did have a tow, from Hamilton, by dint of the fact it was the Monegasque's turn to go out second in final qualifying.
Leclerc qualified second behind dominant Mercedes polesitter George Russell, who topped qualifying by a season-high margin of eight tenths of a second.
Reflecting on his own session, Hamilton told Sky Sports F1: "It was a pretty bad qualifying once again. It's not for the lack of trying.

articles.title: Northridge cheer brings school spirit to AHSAA regional competition
articles.summary: BIRMINGHAM, Ala. — You can hear their calls echoing through the school halls. The sharp-cut diction pierces with each word, echoed by the loud smacks of blue-and-black signs.
body: Shortly after, a rebound is due. One cheerleader held herself upside down in a handstand while teammates tested her balance by watching her evade an air raid of pom-poms. Across the mat, others broke into a tango while serenading with "High School Musical" tunes. Laughter filled the pauses between repetitions of a routine the Jaguars had run for weeks.
A few hours later, at the AHSAA Central-North Regional at the Birmingham CrossPlex, the Jaguars competition team had to morph all of that energy into true spirit.

Every motion had to match. Stunts had to hit. Voices had to boom. Borderline-scarily happy smiles and intense-yet-kind perkiness had to stay consistent through a routine being watched closely by a line of judges.

That energy has become the defining piece of the squad. Coach Erin Darnell has tried to leave room for those lighthearted moments that feed that infectious brightness while working with a young group that combines cheerleaders from different squads. The younger members, she said, helped push Northridge toward competing and eventually took ownership of the opportunity.

articles.title: Celtic, Rangers appeal stadium closure sanction after fan trouble
articles.summary: Celtic and Rangers have appealed against the Scottish FA sanction ordering the two clubs to play their next home Scottish Cup fixture behind closed doors.
body: The Old Firm sides have also challenged the £100,000 sum they were ordered to pay the opposition club for that match.
The punishment ruled a second match would be behind closed doors if there is any trouble at a Scottish Cup fixture until the end of next season.
It followed their quarter-final meeting last season that ended with fans from both sides clashing on the pitch at Ibrox.
Police Scotland arrested 43 people following the scenes that left officers injured as missiles and pyros were launched.

articles.summary: Sky Sports News' chief reporter Kaveh Solhekol explains the Premier League charges brought against Manchester City, the background to the investigation and the potential punishments, with reports that the process is moving to an appeal.
body: There are reports that an independent tribunal has reached decisions in Manchester City's 115 charges case.

Manchester City have been charged with breaking Financial Fair Play rules over a nine-year period, which started in 2009 and went on until 2018. They have also been charged with failing to co-operate with Premier League investigations into their finances.
When the Premier League charged City in 2023, its press release detailed alleged rules breaches that added up to 115 in number, but it is believed that the actual number is 130.
During the period in question, Man City, who have denied all the charges against them, won the Premier League three times.
